articles.title: Dame Jenni Murray died days after car crash, inquest hears
articles.summary: The former presenter of BBC Radio 4 Woman's Hour died earlier this year, eight days after the collision.
articles.body:
BBC broadcaster Dame Jenni Murray died days after being involved in a car crash in which she was dazzled by headlights, an inquest was told.

Dame Jenni, who was the longest-serving presenter of BBC Radio 4's Woman's Hour, died aged 75 on 12 March, eight days after a collision in north London.

North London area coroner Tony Murphy ruled her cause of death was bronchopneumonia caused by fractures to her rib and sternum fractures sustained in the crash.

A statement from Dr Clare Morkane, a consultant at the Royal Free Hospital where Dame Jenni died after being admitted on 4 March, stated: "Jennifer had been driving when she became dazzled by vehicle lights and collided with two stationary vehicles."

Dr Morkane added: "Following the collision, Jennifer was unable to recall events, exited the vehicle independently and she was conveyed to hospital."

The crash took place near Hampstead Heath, at around 19:45 GMT, the inquest heard.

It resulted in "multiple rib fractures", a fracture to the upper sternum and a collapsed lung.

The broadcaster was initially placed on non-invasive ventilation before being moved to intensive care, but she developed bronchopneumonia.

The Metropolitan Police investigated the crash but closed its investigation with no further action.

Dame Jenni joined Woman's Hour in 1987 and left in 2020.

Vintage moments from the shows she presented included a confrontation with Baroness Margaret Thatcher about her childcare policies, a flirtatious interview with actor Jack Nicholson, challenging Edwina Currie about her affair with then PM John Major, and asking Hillary Clinton how she could forgive her husband Bill's infidelity.

Other highlights included an interview with her favourite singer Joan Baez - "the peak of my career", she once said.

After her death was announced, the then-BBC director general Tim Davie paid tribute to her as "a broadcasting icon", while Radio 4 controller Mohit Bakaya described her as "warm, fearless and beloved by listeners".

Dame Jenni announced on air in 2006 that she had been diagnosed with breast cancer.

As well as speaking to her listeners about her breast cancer diagnosis, she also spoke openly about her weight loss surgery and the menopause.

In 2011, she received a damehood in recognition of her contribution to broadcasting, and also won two Sony Awards and was made a member of the Radio Academy Hall of Fame during her career.

articles.title: GLP-1s may have a host of other health benefits. Just ask these people
articles.summary: Here is what scientists currently know about GLP-1s, and where hype may be getting ahead of the evidence.
articles.body:
Shaquille O'Neal has said a GLP-1-based medication helps him sleep better and feel more energetic after years of struggling with obstructive sleep apnea. Amy Schumer reported better energy, increased libido, and improved perimenopausal symptoms after starting medication as well.

Oprah Winfrey, too, has written that the medication helps her feel "calmer and stronger."

Such experiences reflect a larger shift in how these medications are understood and the range of benefits they may provide. While they were developed to help Type 2 diabetes and later obesity, GLP-1-based medications are now being studied – and, in some cases, approved – for conditions involving the heart, kidneys, liver, sleep and even addiction.

"There are a range of systemic health benefits of GLP-1 medications that are linked to their anti-inflammatory properties, metabolic enhancement and mechanical benefits," said Dr. Robert Kushner, a founder of the American Board of Obesity Medicine and professor emeritus at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine.

While several benefits beyond weight loss are well established, others remain unproven. Here's what scientists currently know so far, and where the hype may be getting ahead of the evidence.

GLP-1 is a gut hormone the body naturally releases after eating. Medications that mimic it produce similar effects, including helping regulate blood sugar , slowing the rate at which food leaves the stomach and acting on the brain and digestive system to reduce hunger and help people feel full sooner and for longer.

This can result in weight loss that produces improvements throughout the body, since excess fat tissue promotes inflammation and insulin resistance and can interfere with organ function. Losing a substantial amount of weight can lower blood pressure, improve blood sugar, reduce liver fat and ease pressure on the airway and joints, said Dr. Melanie Jay, a professor of medicine and population health at NYU Grossman School of Medicine.

While she acknowledged that this can sometimes make it difficult to separate the medication's direct benefits from those stemming from weight loss, "there are probably both weight-dependent and weight-independent effects," she said.

Weight loss isn't the only potential benefit, and represents just one part of the story, Jay stressed.

GLP-1 receptors have also been identified in multiple organs and in blood vessels, where activating them can increase nitric oxide – a molecule that helps blood vessels relax and function properly – while also reducing cell damage and encouraging repair, said Dr. Louis Aronne, director of the Comprehensive Weight Control Center at Weill Cornell Medicine.

"And the hormone can have an impact on many disease entities by also reducing inflammation and by directing the effects on GLP-1 receptors in different organ systems," he added.

Yikes! Your blood sugar crashed. Here's how to avoid that again.

Because of their wide-ranging effects, GLP-1-based medications are being studied for benefits beyond weight management, with the strongest evidence coming from large randomized trials.

Studies like this are important as it "demonstrates that treating obesity can prevent major health outcomes – not just change a number on the scale," Jay said. In multiple trials involving adults with obesity and moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea , a GLP-1 substantially reduced the times breathing slowed or stopped during sleep.

A 2025 trial also found that GLP-1s reduced liver inflammation and improved measures of liver scarring in people with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, or MASH, likely by promoting weight loss, reducing liver fat and improving the body's response to insulin.

"And kidney disease is another area with strong randomized-trial evidence," Jay said.

What about GLP-1s curbing addiction, cancer and fertility problems?

The drugs may also have other positive and far-reaching effects, though the supporting evidence for some remains more limited.

Jay explained that because GLP-1 pathways interact with brain circuits involved in reward and craving, a small trial has found they can reduce alcohol cravings and the amount consumed during a controlled drinking session among adults with alcohol use disorder.

Their purported benefits for addiction similarly "comes from a direct effect of GLP-1" on the brain's reward system and the dopamine signaling involved in motivation and reinforcement, Aronne said. Such benefits "and the magnitude of benefit differ widely from person to person."

Fertility claims require similar restraint. It's "more complicated than some headlines suggest," Jay said. "The evidence for direct reproductive benefits remains limited."

Observational studies have also linked GLP-1 use with lower cancer rates, but such studies have yet to establish cause and effect.

"Cancer claims are perhaps where we need the most caution," Jay said.

Despite many benefits and potential ones, Kushner added that anyone considering one of these medications should understand that the drugs can also cause side effects, are often costly and do not work equally well for everyone. He said researchers still need to better understand "which patients benefit most, at what dose and for how long."

"While all GLP-1 medications still gain FDA approval through the regulatory pathways of weight management or as a treatment for diabetes, their effects certainly transcend these two medical conditions," he said.

articles.title: Popular weight-loss strategy shows surprising potential for chronic pain relief
articles.summary: A study reveals that intermittent fasting reshapes the gut microbiome to strengthen the intestinal lining and block inflammatory compounds from the brain.
articles.body: Intermittent fasting has grown in popularity as a weight-loss strategy, but it could also unlock new ways to manage chronic pain by altering how the gut communicates with the brain. A study published in the journal Brain, Behavior, and Immunity, revealed that the timing of meals affects the gut-brain axis, which is a communication system linking the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system. Intermittent fasting is an eating pattern that focuses on when meals are consumed, typically involving extended periods without food, according to health institutions. DAILY EATING HABIT LINKED TO BETTER BRAIN HEALTH IN OLDER ADULTS, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS Chronic pain, defined by the Cleveland Clinic as pain persisting for longer than three months, is often accompanied by cognitive difficulties and anxiety. While traditional treatments target inflammation or pain-signaling nerves, the new research suggests that meal timing may also influence chronic pain by changing gut bacteria and inflammation throughout the body. Scientists at Zhengzhou University in China examined animal models during fasting cycles. They found that intermittent fasting strengthens the intestinal lining, which prevents inflammatory compounds from leaking into the bloodstream and reaching nervous system tissue. SECRET TO WEIGHT LOSS MAY BE HIDING IN YOUR GUT, NEW STUDY SUGGESTS Analysis of the gut microbiome found that fasting increased levels of a bacterium called Alistipes finegoldii. When researchers administered the live bacteria to animals that were not fasting, they saw similar improvements in pain and cognitive function. POPULAR WEIGHT-LOSS DIET SHOWS SURPRISING IMPACT ON SERIOUS MENTAL HEALTH CONDITION The researchers found that the bacterium produces compounds that the body can convert into hippuric acid, a chemical messenger linked to the observed benefits. At the cellular level, hippuric acid acts on an inflammatory pathway called STING, short for Stimulator of Interferon Genes. When this pathway becomes overactive in the nervous system, it can fuel inflammation that worsens pain and interferes with brain function. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES The study demonstrated that hippuric acid turns down STING activity, quieting inflammatory signaling in the central nervous system and resolving behavioral symptoms. Despite the findings, the research carries a few limitations, the research team acknowledged. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER First, observational and early-stage studies can identify a link between intermittent fasting and changes in gut-brain signaling, but they cannot prove that fasting directly causes those changes. Also, individual responses to intermittent fasting vary based on each person's gut microbiome, underlying health conditions, daily nutrient intake and genetics. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ It can also be challenging for some people to adhere to fasting protocols, as strict eating windows may not be safe or feasible for everyone. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP While fasting is not a cure for chronic pain, researchers said the findings could help guide future treatments that target the gut-brain connection. They added that further trials will be necessary to establish specific dietary protocols tailored to individual patient needs.

articles.title: Three killed in strikes on Gaza as Israel renews threats over kite-flying
articles.summary: Israeli defence minister renews threat to expel Palestinians from areas where kites or balloons are being flown in Gaza.
articles.body:
At least three Palestinians have been killed in separate Israeli attacks on the Gaza Strip, medics and local media reported.

This comes as Israel’s Defence Minister Israel Katz on Thursday renewed his threat to expel Palestinians from any area in Gaza where kites were being flown.

One Palestinian was killed and others injured in an Israeli attack on a tent housing displaced people west of Gaza City on Thursday, a source at Al-Shifa Hospital said.

An Israeli drone strike also hit a tent sheltering displaced people in the al-Mawasi area in western Khan Younis, killing one person and injuring others, the Palestinian Wafa news agency reported.

Separately, an Israeli drone targeted an electric bicycle near the al-Sinaa intersection west of Gaza City, killing one person and injuring several others, including one critically, it added.

The ongoing Israeli attacks come despite a US-brokered “ceasefire” that came into effect in October 2025.

Although major fighting halted in the strip after the agreement, deadly Israeli strikes have continued.

The Israeli military said the latest air strikes in Khan Younis were targeting Hamas fighters. In a post on X, it claimed that a Hamas commander who took part in holding three Israeli hostages was killed in the strikes.

Palestinian authorities accuse Israel of undermining efforts to implement a broader plan by US President Donald Trump to end the genocidal war on Gaza, which includes the full withdrawal of Israeli troops from the strip and disarming Hamas.

Renewed Israeli threats over kite flying

As strikes continue, Katz renewed his threat to expel Palestinians from areas where kites or balloons were being flown in Gaza.

Katz made the threat during a high-level security meeting with Israeli military chief Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir and other top military officials including the head of Israel’s air defence, according to a statement released by his office.

“Based on the instructions of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and my instructions, the Israeli army will use all necessary tools, including evacuating Gaza residents from any area or neighborhood from which [kite and balloon] launches are carried out,” Katz said.

Earlier, Katz said in a post on X, “A balloon and kite shall be treated the same as a drone – with or without explosives”, prompting Palestinian parents to prevent their children from flying kites.

Zamir on Tuesday said plans to demilitarise Gaza and disarm Hamas “using all necessary means” would continue despite recent efforts by the US to advance the ceasefire.

Israeli attacks in Gaza have killed more than 1,300 Palestinians and injured more than 4,000 since the ceasefire came into effect, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry.

The Israeli army has reported five deaths in its ranks over the same period, as well as one civilian contractor.

More than 73,400 Palestinians have been killed and over 174,400 injured in Israeli attacks since the genocidal war began in October 2023.

articles.title: 2 airport workers are dead after malaria cases shock officials at major travel hub
articles.summary: Two employees at Frankfurt Airport in Germany died after six workers contracted airport malaria, prompting mosquito traps and genetic analysis of captured insects.
articles.body: Two employees have died after a cluster of malaria cases emerged among workers at Frankfurt Airport, and officials are investigating mosquitoes at the major German travel hub. Six employees contracted a form of the disease known as "airport malaria" through their work at the airport, Fraport, the company that operates Frankfurt Airport, told Fox News Digital in a statement. Based on a recent update from the Frankfurt Health Department, two of those employees died as a result of the infections, Fraport said. POPULAR NYC MUSEUM TESTS POSITIVE FOR LEGIONNAIRES' DISEASE BACTERIA AMID OUTBREAK "We are shocked and deeply saddened by the loss of our colleagues, and our thoughts are with their families and friends," the company said. The other four affected workers have recovered, according to Fraport, which said its departments are closely monitoring the situation. Malaria is a serious disease caused by a parasite and is most commonly spread to people through the bite of an infected mosquito, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Early symptoms can include fever, chills, headache, muscle aches and fatigue, the CDC said. The disease can become severe or deadly if it is not diagnosed and treated quickly. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "We have provided comprehensive information to all employees and encourage them to consult a doctor if they experience any symptoms," Fraport said. Employees were also advised to tell their doctors that they work at the airport and that cases of airport malaria have been reported there to help ensure appropriate medical examination and treatment, the company said. Mosquito traps have also been installed at the airport, according to the company. Mosquitoes caught in the traps will undergo genetic analysis by the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp, Belgium, to determine their species and origin, Fraport said. The virus can spread between animals and people and can cause symptoms ranging from fever to brain infection and death, according to the Cleveland Clinic. Following the outbreak, Thailand introduced monitoring and screening measures at international travel checkpoints, according to the country's Department of Disease Control. Travelers showing a high fever or symptoms associated with Nipah could face additional screening and be asked to provide their travel history, possible exposure and when their symptoms began, the department said. articles.title: Coroner says baby with measles in Pennsylvania died of a ruptured spleen
articles.summary: After the Pennsylvania Health Department announced that an infant’s death was associated with measles, the coroner involved has said he does not consider measles to be the cause of death.
articles.body: After the Pennsylvania Health Department announced Wednesday that one of the two people whose deaths in the state were associated with measles was an infant, the coroner involved in the case has said he does not consider measles to be the cause of death. The Lancaster County coroner, Dr. Stephen Diamantoni, said in an interview Wednesday evening that the baby died shortly after birth from an internal hemorrhage and “traumatic rupture” of the spleen. He said he found evidence of the measles virus in the infant’s lung tissue. It is still unclear whether measles played a role in the infant’s death. An infection can cause the spleen to enlarge — which raises the risk of rupture — but that could be difficult to detect in an autopsy after a rupture has occurred. Diamantoni, a Republican who has held the elected position since 2008, said he did not find evidence that the infant’s spleen was enlarged. He added that he was investigating the death further, saying the infant was born at a birthing center assisted by a lay midwife who was not certified in midwifery. The health secretary, Dr. Debra Bogen, expressed confidence Wednesday in her department’s conclusion that the death was “measles-associated,” a term that means there was laboratory or epidemiologic evidence of a measles infection. “As a pediatrician with more than 30 years of caring for children, I have thoroughly reviewed the case investigation information and sadly can confirm that there were two recent measles-associated deaths in Lancaster County,” Bogen said in a statement. Gov. Josh Shapiro, a Democrat, nominated her for the role in 2023. The Health Department has not provided details about the second death linked to measles, though it said Tuesday that both people were unvaccinated. Newborns are not eligible for the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine; the first dose is recommended at 12 to 15 months and the second at 4 to 6 years. In Lancaster County, the share of kids who have gotten the MMR vaccine fell from 95.5% in 2017 to 87.6% last year. Generally, a threshold of 95% is considered necessary to maintain herd immunity. The two deaths are the first associated with measles in the U.S. this year and the first in Pennsylvania in 35 years. The state’s Health Department has confirmed 424 measles cases this year, 94 of which were diagnosed in the past week. So far, 73 people have been hospitalized for measles complications in Pennsylvania. Nationwide, 2,777 measles cases have been confirmed this year, the most in 35 years. Dr. Paul Offit, a pediatrician and director of the Vaccine Education Center at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, said two deaths out of 494 reported cases is a stunning number, given that, historically, measles infections cause 1 to 2 deaths per 1,000 cases. “That’s 1 death per 200 people,” Offit said, suggesting the scope of the outbreak may be more dire than official numbers show. “This is much worse than people are saying.”

articles.title: PM é indiciado pela Justiça Militar após atirar contra mecânico no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso aconteceu em Sobradinho, no início de agosto. Baleado passou por cirurgia e sobreviveu. Soldado foi indiciado pelos crimes de abandono de posto e lesão corporal.
articles.summary: Caso aconteceu em Sobradinho, no início de agosto. Baleado passou por cirurgia e sobreviveu.
articles.body:
A Justiça Militar concluiu o inquérito que apurou a conduta do policial militar que atirou contra o proprietário de uma oficina mecânica em Sobradinho , na Região dos Vales no RS. Relembre o caso abaixo.

O soldado Djavan Roger Fritsch foi indiciado pelos crimes de abandono de posto e lesão corporal . O g1 entrou em contato com a defesa do policial, mas não obteve retorno até a publicação desta reportagem.

Fritsch permanece preso preventivamente e está internado na ala psiquiátrica do Hospital da Brigada Militar, em Porto Alegre . Segundo a corporação, ele segue afastado das funções . A Brigada Militar informou que uma eventual retomada das atividades dependerá de avaliações médicas e administrativas.

Paralelamente, Djavan também responde na esfera comum. Ele foi indiciado pela Polícia Civil e denunciado pelo Ministério Público por tentativa de homicídio qualificado e lesão corporal. O caso tramita na Justiça e poderá ser levado a julgamento pelo Tribunal do Júri.

O episódio ocorreu em 1º de agosto. Conforme a investigação, o soldado estava em serviço em Passa Sete quando se deslocou até a oficina do mecânico Willian Wink, em Sobradinho, onde efetuou disparos contra a vítima.

Willian foi encaminhado para um hospital em Cachoeira do Sul , onde passou por cirurgias e ficou internado. Ele deixou a Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) em 17 de agosto, mas continua em recuperação.

PM atira 4 vezes contra dono de oficina mecânica no RS — Foto: Reprodução

Conforme a investigação policial, o PM foi até o local, onde ocorreu uma discussão com o proprietário do estabelecimento. Imagens analisadas pela polícia mostram o momento em que os dois entram em confronto. Em seguida, o policial efetua disparos contra a vítima. Veja vídeo acima.

Segundo a apuração, o conflito entre o policial e o dono da oficina já se arrastava havia cerca de dois anos . O estabelecimento costuma receber reclamações de moradores por conta do barulho provocado durante testes em motocicletas.

Seriam pelo menos sete ocorrências registradas por perturbação de sossego em relação a essa oficina , registradas pela família do PM e por outros moradores. O andamento desses casos não foi informado.

O policial investigado se apresentou à Brigada Militar após o episódio e entregou a arma utilizada . Ele foi encaminhado ao Presídio Policial Militar, em Porto Alegre.

"A Brigada Militar informa, acerca das imagens de câmeras de segurança de um estabelecimento comercial, no município de Sobradinho/RS, que mostram um Militar Estadual efetuando disparos de arma de fogo contra um indivíduo, que o referido Militar Estadual, durante o serviço, após discussão em razão de desavenças pessoais com o indivíduo, efetuou quatro disparos de arma de fogo, sendo que três atingiram a vítima, que foi socorrida e encaminhada ao Hospital de Cachoeira do Sul , onde permanece internada.

Diante dos fatos ocorridos, o Militar Estadual foi autuado em flagrante delito, em razão dos crimes militares em tese praticados, sendo encaminhado ao Presídio Policial Militar, onde ficará à disposição da Justiça Militar do Estado. Em complemento, as investigações prosseguem para o completo esclarecimento de todas as circunstâncias do fato em tela.

A Brigada Militar reforça que pauta sua atuação na imparcialidade, na legalidade e não compactua com qualquer conduta que se revele incompatível com os princípios basilares da Instituição, pautando a atuação de polícia judiciária militar com devido rigor e ética na apuração, assegurando ao investigado o devido processo legal e o direito à ampla defesa."

articles.title: Bruno & Marrone embalam Barretos com sertanejo romântico e sucessos que atravessam gerações | G1
articles.standfirst: Dupla que completa 40 anos de carreira em 2026 abriu noite de shows no Palco Estádio na noite desta quinta-feira (27), no Parque do Peão.
articles.summary: Dupla que completa 40 anos de carreira em 2026 abriu noite de shows no Palco Estádio na noite desta quinta-feira (27), no Parque do Peão.
articles.body:
A voz de milhares de pessoas tomou conta da arena, das arquibancadas e dos camarotes do Parque do Peão, em Barretos (SP), na noite desta quinta-feira (27). Em um dos shows mais aguardados da noite, Bruno & Marrone transformaram o espaço completamente lotado em um grande coro para cantar sucessos que marcaram as quatro décadas de carreira da dupla.

A apresentação no Palco Estádio começou com “Inevitável”, seguida por “Agora” e “Te Amar Foi Ilusão”, em um primeiro bloco que mostrou a força do sertanejo romântico entre o público da Festa do Peão. Antes mesmo de Bruno & Marrone começarem a cantar, os primeiros acordes já eram suficientes para arrancar gritos e fazer os fãs acompanharem cada verso.

“Desde o momento que entramos aqui, nunca mais saímos. E estamos muito felizes em estar mais uma vez com vocês. É um privilégio!”, afirmou Marrone.

Bruno & Marrone são atrações desta quinta-feira (27) na Festa do Peão de Barretos — Foto: Ricardo Nasi/g1

Ao longo da apresentação, a dupla convidou os “corações apaixonados” a cantar junto os grandes sucessos da carreira. E o convite foi prontamente aceito: em músicas como “Se Não Tivesse Ido” e “Choram as Rosas”, o público assumiu os vocais em diversos momentos, formando um coro que podia ser ouvido por toda a arena.

Na sequência, vieram “Por Um Minuto”, “Amor de Carnaval”, “Ligação Urbana” e “Programa de Fim de Semana”. Do início ao fim, os fãs acompanharam as músicas da dupla, mostrando que os sucessos de Bruno & Marrone seguem atravessando gerações.

Além do repertório romântico, a apresentação também teve espaço para brincadeiras. Bruno falou sobre tocar berrante enquanto tomava uma bebida no palco e arrancou risadas do público ao comentar sobre o consumo de álcool.

“Pode beber, mas beba com moderação. Eu entendi que beber com moderação é jantar antes”, brincou.

“Aqui é lugar de beber e ser feliz”, completou Marrone.

Em outro momento, Bruno destacou a importância de estar novamente no palco de Barretos e citou a solidariedade de artistas que, assim como eles, doaram cachês ao Hospital de Amor.

“Só de estarmos aqui hoje, com saúde, cantando, é uma vitória. As maiores atrações aqui doaram seu cachê para o Hospital do Amor. Cantando de graça eu canto até melhor”, disse, aos risos.

Bruno & Marrone cantam sucessos na Festa do Peão de Barretos — Foto: Ricardo Nasi/g1

A dupla também aproveitou o show para bater papo com o público, ouvir pedidos de músicas e descobrir quem era de São Paulo e quem havia vindo de outros estados para acompanhar a Festa do Peão.

“Todos os anos é como se fizéssemos um show novo aqui, é sempre um público diferente”, afirmou Marrone.

Bruno ainda garantiu que a dupla estará em Barretos todos os anos e só deixará de participar da Festa quando parar de cantar.

Também houve espaço para o modão, com Marrone na sanfona. O repertório trouxe clássicos como “Amargurado”, de Tião Carreiro e Pardinho, “Frente a Frente”, de Matogrosso & Mathias, e “Seu Amor Ainda É Tudo”, de João Mineiro e Marciano.

Além de revisitar sucessos da carreira, Bruno & Marrone também aproveitaram a apresentação em Barretos para cantar ao vivo, pela primeira vez, “Evento do Ano”. A música faz parte do projeto “De Volta aos Bares II”.

“Lançar uma música aqui na Festa de Barretos, a maior do segmento, é muito significativo, um pontapé inicial muito importante”, afirmou Bruno.

“Qualquer artista do mundo gostaria de cantar aqui em Barretos e, lá atrás, nós começamos lá fora e chegamos na arena. E, com 40 anos de carreira, estamos aqui quase todos os anos e, hoje, lançando uma música”, completou Marrone.

Bruno & Marrone se apresentam nesta quinta-feira (27) Festa do Peão de Barretos — Foto: Ricardo Nasi/g1

Convidados especiais da noite, Diego & Victor Hugo subiram ao palco para cantar “Facas”, gravada em parceria com Bruno & Marrone, e “Tubarões”.

Enzo Rabelo, filho de Bruno, também fez uma participação especial no show. Juntos, pai e filho cantaram “Pai, por quê?”. Na sequência, ele cantou “Tijolinho por Tijolinho” e “Perfeitinha”.

Sobrinho de Marrone, Pedro encerrou o bloco de participações especiais cantando “Evidências”, sucesso eternizado na voz de Chitãozinho & Xororó.

A dupla encerrou o show com o sucesso “Dormi na Praça”, responsável por projetar os goianos nacionalmente.

“Obrigada a cada um de vocês que participaram desta festa! Fiquem com Deus. A festa continua!”

articles.title: Marido de mulher com doença de Lito cultiva os hobbies que ela tinha | G1
articles.standfirst: Rose Carvalho, de Gaspar (SC) convive com os sintomas da Creutzfeldt-Jakob há mais de dois anos. Marido Luís da Silva saiu do emprego para cuidar dela.
articles.summary: Marido Luís da Silva saiu do emprego para cuidar dela, em Gaspar, SC.
articles.body:
A música, a leitura e as conversas faziam parte dos hobbies de Rose Carvalho, de 59 anos. Moradora de Gaspar (SC), desde 2024 convive com Creutzfeldt-Jakob e perdeu os movimentos e a fala. A doença rara e degenerativa é a mesma do influenciador Lito , conhecido pelo canal "Aviões e Músicas", e é caracterizada pela perda de movimentos e demência.

O marido Luís da Silva, de 61 anos, deixou o emprego para cuidar dela e faz questão de continuar as atividades favoritas da esposa. O casal está junto há 19 anos e mora sozinho.

"Eu boto música, eu leio livros de coisas que ela gostaria de estar lendo, eu converso, tem uma série de coisas que eu faço para estar estimulando ela", contou o marido.

🔎 A doença de Creutzfeldt-Jakob é rara, neurodegenerativa, progressiva e sem cura. O quadro costuma começar com demência, perda de memória e tremores, e evolui com outros sinais neurológicos que afetam diferentes regiões do cérebro simultaneamente.

Rose começou a sentir sintomas, vertigens e tonturas em fevereiro de 2024. A princípio, a família suspeitava de labirintite. Porém, o quadro dela evoluiu rapidamente.

Ela passou a ter dificuldades para falar, perdeu o equilíbrio e começou a cair com frequência. Em busca do diagnóstico, a paciente fez diversos exames e consultas.

O diagnóstico da doença de Creutzfeld-Jakob foi confirmado posteriormente a partir da análise de uma amostra corporal enviada ao Hospital das Clínicas da Universidade de São Paulo (USP).

Atualmente, Rose se alimenta por sonda e respira com auxílio de uma traqueostomia. Ela perdeu os movimentos e a capacidade de falar.

Rose Carvalho, que agora sofre sintomas da doença Creutzfeld-Jacob, e o marido, Luís da Silva — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O marido conta que, antes da doença, Rosa era uma mulher ativa, alegre sempre disposta a ajudar e apaixonada pela vida.

"Ela era uma força da natureza, muito alegre e afetuosa. Ela adorava música, sair para dançar, encontrar pessoas e dar boas risadas. Ela adorava estar na praia, viajar, e filmes. Ela era uma cinéfila de primeira grandeza", descreveu Luís.

Como marido lida com esposa com doença de Creutzfeld-Jakob

Luís contou que a rotina começa por volta das 3h30 e termina perto das 22h. Durante a madrugada, ele ainda acorda algumas vezes para verificar se está tudo bem e, quando necessário, fazer a aspiração das secreções acumuladas nos pulmões da esposa.

Durante o dia, dedica horas para movimentar o corpo de Rose, que não se mexe mais por conta própria. São exercícios para estimular a interação.

Em dias de sol, ele leva a esposa para o jardim, onde ela pode ficar perto das flores, que sempre foram uma de suas paixões.

"Nós estávamos sempre procurando fazer todas as coisas juntos, era uma relação incrível. Não mudou nada, ela está aqui. A Ro que eu conheço está ali e a minha esperança é que uma hora ela desperte", declarou o marido.

Luís largou o emprego de chef de cozinha para cuidar da esposa.

Luís da Silva leva esposa, Rose Carvalho, para passear no jardim junto às flores — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Trata-se de uma doença priônica — causada pela alteração anormal de uma proteína chamada príon, que se multiplica no cérebro e destrói neurônios, deixando no tecido cerebral um padrão de buracos que dá origem ao termo "espongiforme". A enfermidade é rara, progressiva e, até hoje, sem tratamento capaz de reverter ou interromper sua evolução.

Mais de 85% dos casos são da chamada forma esporádica, sem causa e fonte infecciosa conhecida, de acordo com o Ministério da Saúde. Geralmente acomete pessoas com média de idade de 65 anos e já foram relatados casos em pessoas entre os 14 aos 92 anos de idade.

Entre 5% e 15% dos casos são hereditários. Nos demais, menos de 1%, a proteína anormal é transmitida de forma acidental.

Não há cura. Aproximadamente 90% das pessoas acometidas pela doença morrem em um ano.

Segundo levantamento do Ministério da Saúde, o Brasil registrou 547 casos confirmados da enfermidade entre 2005 e 2021 — período que corresponde aos primeiros 17 anos desde que a doença de Creutzfeldt-Jakob passou a integrar a lista de notificações compulsórias.

Casal não consegue arcar com todas as despesas

Após deixar o emprego, Luís ficou sem a fonte de renda dele. O casal tinha uma reserva financeira, mas ela foi usada na busca pelo diagnóstico e outras despesas médicas.

Rose recebe um benefício de um salário mínimo. Porém, as despesas do mês do casal costumam ficar em torno de R$ 5 mil, com remédios, suplementos, fraldas, itens de higiene e consultas médicas, além dos gastos com a casa.

Apesar de receberam uma parte dos insumos do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), a família não consegue pagar todas as despesas e criou uma vaquinha virtual para receber doações .

articles.summary: Sangue novo vai trazer mais energia e dinamismo aos serviços oferecidos à população.
articles.body:
O Município de Montes Claros convocou mais 510 candidatos aprovados no concurso para preenchimento de cargos efetivos da área da Administração (edital nº 02/2024). Para alguns cargos já foram chamados mais candidatos do que o número de vagas disponibilizadas no certame. Para o cargo de Enfermeiro, por exemplo, havia 215 vagas no edital do concurso, mas já foram convocados 240 candidatos aprovados, além de 23 candidatos inscritos como pessoas com deficiência (PcDs). O mesmo acontece com o cargo de Psicólogo: foram disponibilizadas 100 vagas no concurso e já foram convocados 115 candidatos aprovados, além de 10 inscritos como PcDs.

Agora, foram convocados candidatos aprovados para os cargos de Agente Administrativo, Agente Administrativo da Saúde da Família – ESF, Analista de Sistemas, Assistente Social, Contador, Educador Físico, Enfermeiro, Enfermeiro com Especialização em Saúde da Família, Engenheiro Civil, Engenheiro Eletricista, Farmacêutico/Bioquímico, Fiscal Municipal, Fisioterapeuta, Motociclista, Motorista Carteira “D”, Nutricionista, Odontólogo, Odontólogo com Residência em Saúde da Família, Odontólogo – ESF, Orientador Social, Pedagogo, Psicólogo, Psicólogo Saúde Mental e técnicos em Enfermagem, Higiene Dental, Informática, Laboratório e Vigilância Sanitária, além de Médico Anestesiologista, Cardiologista, Clínico – ESF, Clínico Geral, com especialização em Saúde da Família, com Residência em Saúde da Família, do Trabalho, Ginecologista, Oftalmologista, Plantonista Clínico e Psiquiatra.

Os aprovados no concurso ora nomeados estão sendo convocados de forma gradual através de carta enviada ao endereço informado pelo candidato. O concurso (edital nº 02/2024) terá validade de dois anos, prazo que pode ser prorrogado por igual período. A relação dos 510 candidatos convocados está disponível na edição de 14 de agosto do Diário Oficial Eletrônico do Município ( ).

articles.title: US aid cuts threaten Ghana’s child immunisation gains
articles.summary: Ghana faces a $78.2m health funding shortfall as aid cuts put immunisation gains at risk.
articles.body:
Accra, Ghana – Ghana was among the first countries in Africa to introduce the RTS,S malaria vaccine into its routine immunisation programme. In Ghana, Kenya and Malawi, the vaccine was associated with a 13 percent reduction in mortality among children eligible for vaccination, with roughly one in eight deaths averted.

But keeping those gains will require more than the vaccine itself. Health workers still have to reach children, trace those who miss doses and get vaccines safely to communities.

The suspension of United States Agency for International Development (USAID) programmes left Ghana facing an estimated $156m funding gap across affected programmes, including a projected $78.2m shortfall in health. The health funding supported programmes including malaria prevention, maternal and child health, nutrition, family planning and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) services.

The disruption has also raised concerns about the systems that keep routine immunisation running.

A study examining donor withdrawal in northern Ghana found that 75 percent of the districts surveyed reported vaccine delays or irregular supplies. The study also found constraints affecting cold-chain equipment, delivery kits and transport fuel.

Nana Owusu Ensaw, municipal director of health for Akuapim North, said Ghana should use the funding shock to rethink how it pays for healthcare.

“The $78m health funding gap after USAID programme closures is significant, but it is also a chance to rethink healthcare financing in Ghana. The Ghana Medical Trust Fund, or MahamaCares, is already expanding access to specialised care,” Ensaw said.

“The private sector must also step up. With the right partnerships, Ghana can become a medical tourism hub by investing in diagnostics, telemedicine and specialist care. Banks and financial institutions have a critical role to play. They must support these health tourism initiatives with tailored financing packages to attract more players into the sector. We have the talent and the will. Now we need the investment to match.”

John Yabani, the medical director of Banahene Specialist Hospital, said private providers were also prepared to play a larger role.

“Ghana’s healthcare sector is at a pivotal moment. As a specialist hospital, we have already been investing in medical tourism and positioning ourselves to attract patients from across West Africa and the diaspora. The private sector is ready to step in and complement government efforts. With the right support from financial institutions, we can help build a health system that is resilient, self-sufficient and truly world-class.”

But private investment cannot immediately replace the public health infrastructure needed to deliver routine vaccinations, particularly in remote communities.

Not everyone sees the loss of donor funding only as a setback.

A government official who spoke to Al Jazeera on condition of anonymity said he had long been uncomfortable with African countries relying on Western governments to finance basic healthcare.

“For me, this USAID cut is a perfect opportunity for us to put our house in order and utilise our resources to take care of our citizens,” he said.

George Kwame Egeh, cofounder and director of operations at the Humserve Africa Foundation, which provides surgical aid and immunisation support to deprived communities, said his organisation had long advocated greater use of local funding.

“We have always used internally generated funding from colleagues and corporate Ghana to support all health interventions,” Egeh said. “We believe that civil society organisations (CSOs) can step in and fill the gap that the USAID cuts are creating.”

For immunisation programmes, however, replacing donor money is not simply a matter of finding another funding source. Health workers still have to travel to remote communities, trace children who miss doses, maintain cold-chain equipment and organise outreach services.

‘No child should be denied life-saving immunisation’

In the Oti Region, where many communities are rural, hard to reach and close to Ghana’s borders, the concern is particularly acute.

A 2025 study of routine immunisation in Ghana’s Eastern and Oti regions found basic antigen coverage in Oti of 85.3 percent, while coverage for the national schedule was 62.1 percent.

Mark Appiah, chairman of the Oti Regional Health Committee, told Al Jazeera he was concerned that financing pressures could erode those gains.

“Funding pressures could affect outreach, defaulter tracing, transportation, supervision and immunisation campaigns, all of which are essential to maintaining these gains,” he said.

“A child should not lose protection against a preventable disease because the health system is experiencing a financing problem.”

Appiah said the committee was focusing on domestic resource mobilisation, community participation and targeted support for hard-to-reach communities. He also called for an Oti Regional Health Development and Resource Mobilisation Framework to build structured partnerships with businesses, development partners and NGOs.

For families in communities that can be difficult for health teams to reach, those systems can determine whether a child receives a vaccine or misses a dose.

In northern Ghana, Rahinatu, a mother whose child has benefitted from routine immunisation, said the funding gap had created real challenges for her community.

“But I am optimistic the government will figure a homegrown solution as soon as possible to get things back on track for us,” she said.

Her hope comes as Ghana faces a longer-term shift in how it finances vaccines.

Ghana is in an accelerated transition from Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, support and is expected to take full responsibility for financing its immunisation programme from 2030.

At the same time, Gavi is facing its own funding pressures. The alliance’s 2026–2030 strategy aims to strengthen the financial sustainability of immunisation programmes and increase countries’ domestic contributions as they transition from Gavi support.

That puts Ghana under pressure from two directions: the immediate disruption caused by the withdrawal of US funding and the longer-term need to take on a greater share of immunisation costs.

Ghana has begun looking for ways to do that. The government has removed the cap on funding from the National Health Insurance Scheme, while it is also backing efforts to develop local vaccine manufacturing capacity.

As health ministers and senior officials from the World Health Organization (WHO) African Region’s 47 member states meet in Addis Ababa for the 76th session of the WHO Regional Committee for Africa, Ghana’s experience points to a difficult question facing many countries: how quickly can governments build greater financial independence without allowing the health services that children rely on today to weaken?

“No child in Oti Region should be denied life-saving immunisation because of where that child lives or because of a temporary financing gap.”

articles.title: DRC begins vaccinating front-line healthcare workers against Ebola
articles.summary: Trials for a vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain are ongoing as DRC authorities try to control the Ebola outbreak.
articles.body:
The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has begun vaccinating people against Ebola, with health workers and other front-line workers being prioritised.

However, the vaccine being distributed this week is licensed for another strain, and its effectiveness against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola has not been determined.

There is currently no approved vaccine or treatment for the new strain, and clinical trials are ongoing to find a suitable vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain.

The first injections are being given to health workers in the Congolese city of Kisangani.

More than 50,000 doses of the vaccine have been received, according to the Congolese health minister, Samuel Roger Kamba.

The outbreak is concentrated in the Ituri province, which borders Uganda.

Kamba said: “We will cover all the provinces that are around Ituri, moving in the ring towards the centre of the outbreak.”

The World Health Organization (WHO) said last week that 70,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine had been approved for use in the DRC.

About 20,000 of the doses allocated to the DRC will be used in a clinical trial to test its effectiveness against the latest strain. Health workers are calling for more doses.

As of Tuesday, the DRC had recorded 5,713 confirmed cases of Ebola, including 2,744 deaths, according to government figures. The outbreak is the deadliest of all past Ebola outbreaks that have hit the DRC.

The outbreak is spreading under extremely difficult conditions, fuelled by insecurity, displacement, a health workers’ strike and intense population movements.

The WHO has said it remains out of control and is on track to surpass the 2014-2016 West Africa Ebola outbreak, the deadliest on record, which killed more than 11,000 people, primarily in Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

articles.title: 200 operations cancelled In Jersey amid 'extreme' summer heat
articles.summary: Jersey's health service says "significant work" had been undertaken to minimise the impact.
articles.body:
Approximately 200 elective procedures have been cancelled in Jersey over the summer months due to the failure of chiller units in operating theatres, hospital bosses have said.

The scale of cancellations at Jersey Hospital has been confirmed in a report to August's meeting of the island's healthcare oversight board .

Managing director Andy Weir said efforts had been made to "minimise and manage the disruption", but acknowledged staff had been working in "far from ideal circumstances".

The board agreed on "further work to assess resilience" and said a post-incident review was underway.

In his submission to the health board, Weir said the summer had been "characterised by high and extreme temperatures".

He said the "failure of chiller units" in May, followed by a second chiller failure in June, were responsible for the number of cancellations.

Three operating theatres were closed temporarily because of the issue.

Weir also noted "excessive temperatures across the estate, including on Robin and Orchard wards.

He said hospital teams had worked hard to "mitigate the issues arising from continued hot weather".

Weir said a "targeted recovery programme" was underway to "minimise the impact" of summer disruption on waiting times, however "scheduled theatre ventilation maintenance" would affect it.

A report detailing the impact of the hot weather on services said the May heatwave had "highlighted the increasing vulnerability of the estate to extreme weather events".

It said while "clinical services were maintained safely", the associated risks could not be fully eliminated until a new hospital was in operation.

The board expressed concerns about the "ageing hospital estate" and agreed there would be more work to assess "options to improve estate and equipment resilience".

In a separate financial statement to the board, it was noted the "lack of cooling system resilience" would have a financial knock-on, with "fewer private patient procedures performed, and therefore income collected".

articles.title: Death toll from Nepal-Tibet flood passes 470 as barrier lake threatens
articles.summary: Over 1,500 people remain missing as rescue paused near the Nepal-China border amid fears of further flooding.
articles.body:
The death toll from the flash flood that devastated Nepal and the Tibet region has risen past 470, as rescue efforts continue on both sides of the Himalayan border.

Nepal’s Prime Minister’s Office reported on Friday that 469 people had been confirmed killed and that 977 remain missing. At least three people were killed in Tibet and 558 remain missing, according to Chinese authorities.

In Nepal, 644 of the missing are foreigners, the authorities report. Around 1,550 people have been rescued.

The disaster struck on Wednesday, when a glacier collapse sent a surge of ice, rock and mud down Himalayan river valleys, burying entire villages and destroying roads, bridges and hydropower plants.

Bishal Nath Upreti, president of the Nepal Centre for Disaster Management, told Al Jazeera that the situation was “extremely difficult” for those stranded in the disaster zone, with no road to access them.

“Almost 42km [26 miles} of road is completely wiped out, and, except the helicopters, the rescuers cannot go there”, he said.

About 800 people have been rescued by helicopter and some 700 by land, he said. Aid to survivors is being airlifted to them.

“They are very desperate now,” he said of those stranded. “It’s already over 72 hours now and people are really desperate for … shelter and food.”

Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu, reporting from Beijing, said the number of missing was expected to climb. Nepal has deployed 30,000 security personnel to search remote valleys.

China has deployed about 500 military and paramilitary personnel and sent Premier Li Qiang to supervise operations, she reports.

“That is very, very rare and it really gives us a sense of how urgent and how much of a priority this operation has become.”

Rescue efforts are now being complicated by fears that secondary flooding could impact the disaster zone.

Attention is turning to a newly-formed barrier lake straddling the Nepal-China border. Both countries have warned it is unstable and at risk of bursting.

Barrier lakes form when flooding or landslides block a river, trapping a growing body of water behind a natural dam of debris.

Chinese authorities warned that the lake held around 2 million cubic meters (70 million cubic feet) of water, and was expected to receive another 3 million cubic meters (106 million cubic feet) over the next three days.

Meanwhile, rescue and military teams trying trying to reach the border port of Gyirong, where buildings lie buried under mud 1.5 metres deep, have been ordered to pause their work over fears of a mud slide, Yu reports.

“What this also introduces is a sort of anxious ticking clock,” Al Jazeera’s Yu reports, with teams racing to find survivors and recover bodies before more mud makes the operation more dangerous.

Nepal’s Foreign Ministry said on Friday that the country did not require international assistance with the search.

“The offer for help is natural. Our security agencies are doing the search and rescue operation. For now we don’t require such help,” spokesperson Lok Bahadur Chhetri said.

Al Jazeera’s Minelle Fernandez, reporting from Kathmandu, said Nepal was not entirely spurning offers of help, but had decided on the advice of its military and police that it could handle the initial rescue work itself.

“They have appealed for other forms of aid, for maybe cash disbursements, because obviously this is a mammoth task,” she said.

Standing near Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, she said crowds had gathered around the facility to inquire about missing loved ones.

“Everyone is fighting for answers, waiting for some glimmer of hope, and right now that’s hard to come by,” Fernandez said.
